newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dollar closes firmer in thin but nervous market.
newsitem.headline: NZ dollar closes firmer in thin but nervous market.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar closed firmer on Tuesday in a thin market and dealers see it remaining firm overnight.
The market is nervous about the looseness of monetary conditions.
It ended at US$0.6846/53 at 5.00 p.m. (0500 GMT) from its 0.6826/33 opening while the Trade-Weighted Index recovered to 67.10 from its 67.01 opening.
In the afternoon session, the Kiwi was held to a five basis point range with just one local seller ranged against a local buyer.
There was selling interest from the Asian branches of U.S. investment houses.
Dealers expect it to remain in a 0.6840-65 range overnight.

One said that with the Monetary Conditions Index hovering around 126 basis points weaker that the Reserve Bank's desired level set in March, the index is seen as the outer extreme of the bank's tolerance level.
"The market has probably realised they can't take too much of an easing into this Monetary Policy Statement," he said.
Economists on average expect the bank in its statement on Friday to sanction rates to be 75 basis points easier than the level set in March.
Some dealers expect a classic "sell the rumour, buy the fact" scenario for the MPS.
"I think the market is going into the statement pretty short and you will get a squeeze back to 0.6910 level and then we will work our way lower," one said.
